items.title: Iran rejects Trump's 48-hour ultimatum as Gulf strikes widen

featured_image.name: Kuwait desalination plant, oil refinery hit by missile and drone strikes

items.description:
Iran's central military command on Saturday dismissed President Donald Trump's 48-hour ultimatum to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or face the destruction of its critical infrastructure, as Tehran continued launching waves of drone and missile strikes across the Gulf and at Israel in the latest escalation of the five-week-old war.

General Ali Abdollahi Aliabadi, representing Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, called Trump's threat "a helpless, nervous, unbalanced and stupid action," and warned: "The simple meaning of this message is that the gates of hell will open for you." Trump had written on Truth Social earlier Saturday: "Time is running out — 48 hours before all Hell will reign down on them. Glory be to GOD!"[1][2][3]

items.title: Meloni offers to help rebuild Qatar's war-damaged gas infrastructure

featured_image.name: Italy's Meloni meets Qatar emir to discuss energy issues amid Iran war

items.description:
Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni met with Qatari Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani at Lusail Palace in Doha on Saturday, offering Italy's support to rebuild Qatar's damaged energy infrastructure as Europe grapples with an energy crisis triggered by the US-Israeli war on Iran.[1][2]

Meloni is the first leader from the European Union, NATO, and the G20 to visit the Gulf region since the conflict began on February 28. The unannounced two-day tour, which started in Saudi Arabia on Friday with a meeting with Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, will also include the United Arab Emirates.[3][4][5]

items.title: Iran's military warns Israeli embassies are 'legitimate targets'

featured_image.name: Iran's Khatam al-Anbiya Headquarters details Waves 91 & 92 of “Al-Waad  Al-Sadiq 4”

items.description: Iran's top military command issued a stark warning on Saturday that any Israeli attack on Iranian embassies or diplomatic facilities would prompt retaliatory strikes on Israeli diplomatic sites across the Middle East, escalating rhetoric amid an ongoing military conflict between Iran and a US-Israeli coalition.

items.title: Iran's grip on Strait of Hormuz fuels growing recession fears worldwide

featured_image.name: The Oil Shock Is Here. And We're Just Beginning to Feel It.

items.description: A grinding war in Iran and the effective closure of the Strait of Hormuz have sent oil prices surging and rattled financial markets worldwide, intensifying fears that the global economy may be headed for a recession. With crude benchmarks trading well above $100 a barrel and bond yields falling, Wall Street is signaling that the risk of economic contraction now outweighs concerns about inflation.

items.title: Trump warns Iran of 'hell' as search for downed jet crew enters day 2

featured_image.name: Trump says Iran has 48 hours to make deal as search for US pilot continues

items.description: President Donald Trump dismissed the loss of an American F-15E Strike Eagle fighter jet over Iran on Friday, telling NBC News in a phone interview that the incident would have no bearing on ongoing diplomatic efforts with Tehran. "No, not at all. No, it's war. We're in war, Garrett," Trump told NBC News correspondent Garrett Haake, in his first public remarks on the shootdown.[1][2][3]

items.title: Trump aides advise striking Iran's infrastructure as Monday deadline nears

featured_image.name: Trump extends pause on attacking Iran energy facilities to April 6

items.description:
Senior Trump administration officials have privately advised President Donald Trump that striking Iran's energy and power infrastructure constitutes a legitimate military target, according to The Wall Street Journal, as the U.S.-Iran war enters its sixth week with a critical deadline just two days away.[1][2]

The reporting comes as Trump's self-imposed April 6 deadline for Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz or reach a deal approaches on Monday evening. On Saturday, Trump reiterated his ultimatum on Truth Social, warning that "all hell" would rain down on Iran if it fails to comply within 48 hours.[3][4]

items.title: Israel warns it will strike Lebanon-Syria border crossing

featured_image.name: Key Lebanon–Syria border crossing destroyed by Israeli attack

items.description: The Israel Defense Forces carried out simultaneous waves of strikes across Iran and Lebanon over the weekend, hitting more than 200 Iranian targets and over 140 Hezbollah positions as the five-week-old Operation Roaring Lion continued to expand in scope. The IDF also confirmed the death of another soldier in southern Lebanon, bringing the toll to 11 since ground operations began on March 16.[1][2][3]

items.title: Houthis claim joint strike with Iran on Ben Gurion Airport

featured_image.name: Houthi missile strike at Israel airport halts flights - NPR

items.description:
Yemen's Houthi movement claimed Saturday that it struck Ben Gurion Airport near Tel Aviv and military targets in southern Israel using a fragmentation ballistic missile and attack drones, in what the group described as a joint operation with Iran's Revolutionary Guard, the Iranian army, and Hezbollah in Lebanon.[1][2]

Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree said in a prerecorded statement that the group had "successfully struck Lod Airport (Ben Gurion) in the occupied Jaffa area" along with what he called vital military targets in southern occupied Palestine. "This operation was a joint operation with the Revolutionary Guard, the Iranian army, and Hezbollah in Lebanon, and it successfully achieved its objectives," Saree said.[1]

items.title: Iran launches 95th wave of strikes on U.S. bases across Gulf

featured_image.name: Patriot missile involved in Bahrain blast likely US-operated, analysis finds

items.description: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps carried out a sweeping series of strikes on Saturday targeting U.S. military positions in Kuwait, Bahrain, and the United Arab Emirates, marking the 95th wave of Operation True Promise 4 since the war began five weeks ago. The Iranian Navy also claimed to have set ablaze an Israeli-linked commercial vessel near the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Drone strikes wound 3 at BP-run oilfield in Iraq

featured_image.name: Operations halted at Iraq gas field after shock drone strike

items.description: Two drones struck the BP-operated North Rumaila oilfield in southern Iraq on Saturday, wounding three Iraqi workers, as a separate drone targeted offices belonging to American energy services company KBR at the nearby Majnoon oil field, underscoring the continued vulnerability of Iraq's energy infrastructure more than a month into the broader conflict between the United States, Israel, and Iran.

items.title: Jerusalem's Old City marks quiet Easter as Iran war enters sixth week

featured_image.name: Jerusalem heads into a subdued Passover and Easter under the shadow of the Iran  war

items.description: Jerusalem's Old City, normally bustling with pilgrims and tourists during the spring holiday season, has fallen nearly silent as Passover and Easter coincide under the shadow of the ongoing war between Iran and the U.S.-Israeli coalition. Metal shutters line the stone alleyways, holy sites stand largely empty, and the few worshippers who come do so under strict military guidelines that have transformed one of the world's most sacred quarters into a ghost town.[1][2]

items.title: Russia evacuates 198 workers after strike near Iran's Bushehr nuclear plant kills one

featured_image.name: Projectile hits near Iran’s Bushehr nuclear plant, killing one: IAEA

items.description: A projectile struck near Iran's Bushehr nuclear power plant on Saturday morning, killing a security guard and damaging an auxiliary building in what the International Atomic Energy Agency confirmed was the fourth such incident since the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran began on February 28.

items.title: Hezbollah rocket hits Kiryat Shmona without warning sirens as Lebanon war intensifies

featured_image.name: ISRAEL-LEBANON-IRAN-US-WAR

items.description:
A Hezbollah rocket struck a residential area of Kiryat Shmona on Saturday without warning sirens activating, damaging buildings and infrastructure in the northern Israeli border town, as cross-border fighting between Israel and the Lebanese militant group intensified on multiple axes.[1][2][3]

The strike, which caused no reported casualties, prompted an investigation by the Israel Defense Forces into the failure of its alert systems. It came amid a day of sustained Hezbollah barrages targeting northern Israeli communities, with the group claiming it hit Kiryat Shmona at least seven times on Friday alone using rockets and loitering drones. Hezbollah also claimed attacks on Israeli troop concentrations in the border towns of Marun al-Ras, Hula, Ainata, and Bayada in southern Lebanon.[4][5][6][1]

items.title: Jerusalem's holy sites empty as Iran war upends Easter, Passover

featured_image.name: Jerusalem heads into a subdued Passover, Easter under the shadow war

items.description:
Jerusalem's Old City, normally teeming with pilgrims during the overlapping spring holidays, has fallen near-silent this year as the Iran-Israel war enters its sixth week, upending Easter and Passover observances in one of the world's holiest places.

Since the start of the U.S.-Israel military operation against Iran on February 28, Israeli authorities have barred access to the Old City for anyone other than residents and shop owners, according to the Times of Israel. Shops along the ancient stone streets sit shuttered under Home Front Command directives, and holy sites including the Western Wall, Al-Aqsa Mosque, and the Church of the Holy Sepulchre have been closed to the general public since March 6. Nationwide, gatherings remain limited to 100 people indoors and 50 outdoors, provided a bomb shelter can be reached within 90 seconds.[1][2][3]

items.title: Strikes on Iran's Mahshahr petrochemical zone kill 5, wound 170

featured_image.name: US and Israel strike petrochemical facilities in southwest Iran

items.description: US and Israeli airstrikes struck the Mahshahr Special Petrochemical Economic Zone in southwestern Iran on Saturday, killing at least five people and wounding 170 others in an attack targeting one of the country's most important industrial hubs. The Israel Defense Forces confirmed responsibility for the strikes, saying the complex housed "one of the primary locations where a critical component for ballistic missiles is produced."[1][2]

items.title: Artemis II crew fixes frozen toilet line on way to Moon

featured_image.name: NASA Answers Your Most Pressing Artemis II Questions

items.description: Four astronauts aboard NASA's Orion spacecraft are now more than halfway to the Moon on a historic mission, though an intermittent toilet malfunction has added an unscripted challenge to humanity's first lunar voyage in more than half a century.

items.title: Nine-spin quantum system outperforms classical AI in weather forecasting

featured_image.name: Using Quantum Computing to Tell the Weather

items.description:
A quantum processor made from just nine atomic spins has beaten classical neural networks containing thousands of nodes at predicting real-world weather patterns, in what researchers describe as the first experimental demonstration of a quantum machine learning system outperforming large-scale classical models on a practical task.

The study, published in Physical Review Letters on Friday, was led by scientists at the University of Science and Technology of China in Hefei, with collaborators at Fudan University, the Chinese University of Hong Kong, and Zhejiang University.[1][2][3]

items.title: Hezbollah launches 60 attacks as Israeli strikes kill civilians in Lebanon

featured_image.name: Israeli attacks on southern Lebanon kill two girls, damage hospital

items.description: Fighting between Israel and Hezbollah intensified on Saturday as the Lebanese militant group struck an Israeli Merkava tank with a guided missile in southern Lebanon, setting it ablaze, while Israeli airstrikes killed at least two girls and wounded 40 people across the country's south, according to Lebanon's health ministry.[1][2]

items.title: Iran rejects Pakistan-led ceasefire talks with U.S., threatens second shipping chokepoint

featured_image.name: Iran's parliament speaker hints at targeting Bab el-Mandeb Strait

items.description: Diplomatic efforts to halt the widening conflict between the United States and Iran collapsed on Friday after Tehran formally rejected a Pakistan-brokered mediation initiative, refusing to send officials to Islamabad and dismissing Washington's demands as "unacceptable," according to The Wall Street Journal. The breakdown leaves no clear path to a ceasefire as violence in the region intensifies and global shipping through the Strait of Hormuz remains paralyzed.[1]

items.title: Israeli airstrike kills one in Gaza as ceasefire violations mount

featured_image.name: Israeli air strikes on Gaza kill four Palestinians - Al Jazeera

items.description:
Israeli forces struck a civilian vehicle at the entrance of the al-Maghazi refugee camp in central Gaza on Saturday evening, killing one Palestinian man and injuring several others who were transported to Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in Deir al-Balah, according to the Palestinian news agency WAFA. The Middle East Monitor reported three others were wounded in the attack on Salah al-Din Street.[1][2]

The strike came on what Palestinian authorities count as the 177th day since the ceasefire agreement between Israel and Hamas took effect in October 2025. Despite the deal, Israeli forces have continued near-daily airstrikes, drone attacks, artillery shelling, and naval fire across the Strip.
